summary: Windy Peak lookout in Lane County, Oregon, built 1938 as a 50-foot tower and destroyed in a 1958 windstorm; BLM closed the access road in 2024 for two years.

facts.status_note: Destroyed in a 1958 windstorm; no source describes what remains
facts.agency: Bureau of Land Management (administrator per the register)

access.note: BLM closed Windy Peak Road to vehicles after a landslide in November 2024, planned for two years; the release does not mention the lookout

events.note: Road completed and work on the 50-foot tower started, September 1937
Five-man Forest Service crew did general maintenance, including lightning protection
Activated March 16, 1942, with the Eugene Filter Center listed beside the date
Two women went up to relieve the observers for a week in April 1943
May 1944 Aircraft Warning Service report lists post William 9-1; Forest Service kept the station for fire detection when that service ended
June 1949 item names Jack Francis of Michigan State University as the only new lookout, with his wife and small son
BLM closed Windy Peak Road to vehicles after a landslide, planned for two years

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The register names only the Bureau of Land Management. firelookout.com pairs the Siuslaw National Forest with the BLM. The Oregon Lookouts page shows the Forest Service ran the lookout in the 1940s. The story uses the register for current administration and notes the earlier Forest Service role.

sources.title: BLM Closes Windy Peak Road Following Landslide
sources.publisher: Bureau of Land Management news release, reprinted by The Ashland Chronicle

notes_for_editor: Brief's height (50 ft, 15.2 m) and BLM agency are consistent with the register; no correction needed. The 1941, 1943 and 1949 newspaper items are quoted through the Oregon Lookouts transcriptions, not the original papers. The 2024 BLM release closes Windy Peak Road but never names the lookout, so the story does not say the closure blocks the site. A two-year closure from November 2024 would run to about November 2026; that end date is not verified. Web search found no current status for the summit.
